Record date: 2129-04-10
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 04/10/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Increased shortness of breath, persistent edema, and worsening anxiety.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for follow-up two weeks after his previous visit. He reports a continued decline in his respiratory status, with persistent shortness of breath even during minimal exertion, such as walking from his living room to the kitchen. He describes episodes of increased wheezing and has noted a change in his sputum, which is now occasionally yellowish. Mr. Fairfax has been using his nebulizer four times daily, in addition to his albuterol inhaler, which he uses approximately eight times daily.
The bilateral lower extremity edema remains significant, with Mr. Fairfax reporting that he now has difficulty fitting into his shoes. He has gained an additional 3 pounds since the last visit, bringing his total weight gain over the past month to 5 pounds. He expresses frustration and concern regarding the swelling and its impact on his mobility and quality of life.
Mr. Fairfax's anxiety persists, exacerbated by his worsening physical health. He reports increased difficulty sleeping, with only a few hours of unbroken sleep each night. He has been utilizing relaxation techniques learned in therapy but feels they have been insufficient in managing his anxiety levels.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + weight gain, + fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + increased dyspnea with exertion, + nocturnal wheezing, + productive cough with yellowish sputum, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain, + persistent bilateral lower extremity edema. Neurological - + increased anxiety, + insomnia, no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, currently using eight times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 2 puffs twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 200 mg daily (considering increase). 7. Sertraline 200 mg daily (recently increased). 8. Prednisone 40 mg daily for COPD exacerbation (completed course).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.7F, HR 84, BP 145/92, RR 30, O2 sat 76% on room air.
General: Elderly male in moderate respiratory distress, appears fatigued and anxious. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, marked wheezing noted on expiration, some rhonchi present. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 3+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 9.5, Hgb 9.9, Hct 28.5, Plt 215. 2. BMP: Na 132, K 4.5, Cl 95, CO2 22, BUN 60, Cr 3.5, Glucose 88. 3. BNP: 950 (further elevated). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 2.9 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax's respiratory condition continues to deteriorate, and he is referred to pulmonary medicine for advanced management, including consideration for long-term oxygen therapy. A sputum culture will be obtained to assess for possible infection given the change in sputum color. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. The serum creatinine has worsened, necessitating an urgent nephrology consultation to evaluate renal function and adjust diuretic therapy as needed. 3. Lower extremity edema: The persistent edema remains a concern. Furosemide dosage will be increased to 80 mg twice daily, and dietary sodium restrictions will be reinforced. Daily weight monitoring is crucial to assess response to the increased diuretic. 4. Mental health: Mr. Fairfax's anxiety and insomnia have not improved adequately. A referral to psychiatry for medication management is expedited, and continuation of cognitive-behavioral therapy is encouraged.
Patient education was reinforced regarding the importance of recognizing exacerbation signs, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to manage COPD and edema effectively.
